T007.en: You can see Colmar's main sights in a couple of hours. The question is what you want to take away from the visit: photos of façades, or a better understanding of what you've seen.

T008.en: The town is compact: the old town's best-known buildings are a few minutes' walk from each other, and you can cover them in a morning. That's why Colmar is easy to fit into an Alsace itinerary even for half a day. But if you want not just to see but to understand what you're looking at, some context makes a difference. Our old-town audio guide — 27 stops, about an hour and a half — turns a walk from sight to sight into a walk through the town's history.

T009.en: Everything else about the town is in our complete guide to Colmar.

T026.en: What Colmar is like in practice

T027.en: Colmar's historic centre is protected, much of it is pedestrian, and it's often called an open-air museum. The Maison des Têtes, the Maison Pfister, the Koïfhus, St Martin's Church — all within walking distance. For context: the tourist office's official walking trail around town is 6.1 km, about 2 hours 30 minutes, with 40 points of interest. You can see the essentials of the historic centre in less time.

T028.en: Around it lies Alsace: the Wine Route, villages, castles. Colmar is a convenient starting point for all of it. So the answer to "how many days" doesn't depend on the town alone.

T030.en: Half a day is enough to walk the old town and Little Venice. If you have time left, add a canal boat trip or the little tourist train: a loop takes about 35 minutes.

T031.en: If you try to add the Unterlinden Museum to an old-town walk in half a day, you'll have to pick up the pace: its collections span almost 7,000 years of history — from prehistory to 20th-century art, including the Isenheim Altarpiece — and it can easily take up a part of the day on its own. More in our guide to Colmar's museums.

T043.en: One day is enough to see Colmar's essentials at a relaxed pace. In a day you can combine the old town, lunch and one more thing — a museum, say, or a boat trip. How to put that day together will be covered in our guide to one day in Colmar.

T044.en: If you want to add villages or the Wine Route without rushing, plan an extra day.

T046.en: Staying over lets you see Colmar early in the morning and in the evening, outside the busiest daytime hours.

T047.en: In December an overnight stay makes particular sense: Colmar at Christmas really comes into its own after dark. For the markets themselves, see Colmar Christmas markets; for where to stay, see where to stay in Colmar.

T048.en: Day two: Colmar as a base

T049.en: From day two, Colmar works well as a base for exploring Alsace.

T050.en: Museums. The Unterlinden Museum, the Bartholdi Museum and others — whatever didn't fit into day one.

T051.en: Villages. Eguisheim, Riquewihr, Kaysersberg, Turckheim — each with its own character.

T052.en: The Wine Route. The Wine Route and the vineyards start right on Colmar's doorstep.

T053.en: Castles and other trips. Hohlandsbourg above Colmar, Haut-Koenigsbourg, the fortified town of Neuf-Brisach.

T054.en: With three days you can combine the town with one or two regional trips without rushing. And for how to get here, see how to get to Colmar.

T055.en: Who will love it — and who won't

T056.en: You'll love it if you enjoy compact historic towns, architecture, Alsatian food and wine, and don't mind walking a lot.

T057.en: It may disappoint if you're after a big city with endless things to do. Colmar is small, and during major seasonal events the historic centre can get crowded. If you want a bigger city, compare Colmar with Strasbourg.

T058.en: And behind the façades lies the complex Franco-German history of Alsace. More on that in our article on why Colmar looks both French and German.

T060.en: Trying to see both the old town and the Unterlinden in detail in half a day. You can combine them, but you'll have to speed up; for an unhurried visit, allow a full day.

T061.en: Trying to see Colmar and several wine villages in one unhurried day. If you want to add the region, plan an extra day.

T062.en: Driving into the centre. The old town is largely pedestrian. Where to leave the car: see parking in Colmar.

T065.en: Colmar suits people who enjoy compact historic towns, Alsatian architecture, food and wine. If you're after a big city with a wider range of things to do, Colmar may feel too compact — compare it with Strasbourg.

T066.en: How many days do you need in Colmar?

T067.en: Allow one day for the town's essentials. An overnight stay adds the evening and early morning; two or three days make sense if you want to add museums, villages and the Wine Route.

T068.en: Can you see Colmar in half a day?

T069.en: The old town and Little Venice, yes. There won't be much time left for museums.

T070.en: Can you do Colmar as a day trip from Strasbourg?

T071.en: Yes: Colmar has direct trains to and from Strasbourg. More in how to get to Colmar.

T073.en: It depends on what you're looking for. We'll compare the two in a separate article.
